p: ten times have ye reproached me: That is, many times, as in Ne 4:12.
remaineth with myself: That is, I myself will be punished for it, or you have not yet consulted it.
overthrown me: He breaks out again into his passions and declares still that his affliction comes from God though he is not able to feel the cause in himself.
pass: Meaning, out of his afflictions.
crown from my head: Meaning, his children, and whatever was dear to him in this world.
a tree: Which is plucked up, and has no more hope to grow.
troops come together: His manifold afflictions.
They that dwell in mine house: My household servants by all these losses Job shows that touching the flesh he had great opportunity to be moved.
own body: Which were hers and mine.
cleaveth to my skin and to: Besides these great losses and most cruel unkindness, he was touched in his own person as follows.
pity upon me: Seeing I have these just causes to complain, condemn me not as a hypocrite, especially you who should comfort me.
God: Is it not enough that God punishes me, unless you by reproaching increase my sorrow?
flesh: To see my body punished, unless you trouble my mind?
an iron pen and lead in: He protests that despite his sore passions his religion is perfect and that he in not a blasphemer as they judged him.
redeemer liveth: I do not so justify myself before the world, but I know that I will come before the great judge who will be my deliverer and Saviour.
in my flesh shall I see: In this Job declares plainly that he had a full hope, that both the soul and body would enjoy the presence of God in the last resurrection.

matter is found in me: Though his friends thought that he was only persecuted by God for his sins, yet he declares that there was a deeper consideration that is, the trial of his faith and patience, and so to be an example for others.
punishments of the sword: God will be avenged of this harsh judgment by which you condemned me.
